content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I hope you are all well. I have a question regarding a [product_name] PLC used to control the level in a tank. I would like to set up a backup [product_name] PLC of the same type to ensure that if PLC1 fails, control would automatically switch to PLC2. Could you advise what changes should be made in the program or hardware to achieve this goal? I am using [product_name] PLCs with article number [article_no]. Looking forward to your helpful responses.

Since this question relates to network inputs and outputs, it appears you think your [article_no] [product_name] PLC supports Ethernet or Modbus communication. Actually, this feature is available only from [product_name] [version_no] onward.

Hello [user_name], To achieve redundancy, PLC2 needs to detect when PLC1 has failed. Switching analog inputs and especially outputs should be managed using relays. Additionally, if you're creating a redundant control setup, consider how you'll handle the level sensors as well. Best regards, [user_name] (translated with Google)

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing ways to implement redundancy for a [product_name] PLC system controlling a tank's level. The main inquiry is about ensuring automatic failover to a backup device if the primary one fails. Replies highlight hardware limitations of the user's specific [product_name] ([article_no]), particularly in networking capabilities, and suggest additional considerations for sensor redundancy. The main challenges are guidance on practical redundancy setup and device constraints.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to configure a [product_name] PLC system where a backup unit automatically assumes control if the main device fails, without manual intervention. They are looking for clear instructions regarding necessary programming and hardware changes to realize reliable redundancy.
